intro.text: This entry describes autosomal dominant deafness-55 (DFNA55).

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant deafness-55 is designated DFNA55.
checks.explanation: The paper is a mouse study of Tectb knockout and cochlear tuning. It never mentions DFNA55, autosomal dominant deafness, or any human disease designation.

paragraphs.text: Russell et al. (2007) made Tectb-null mice by deleting exons 1 to 4 of the Tectb gene. In these mice, Tectb protein was absent from the tectorial membrane, and the striated-sheet matrix was missing along the membrane's whole length. The tectorial membrane stayed attached to the organ of Corti. However, Hensen's stripe was absent, the marginal band was lost apically, and the apical tectorial membrane was about twice as thick as in controls.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) generated Tectb-null mice by deleting exons 1 to 4 of the Tectb gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We used gene targeting in embryonic stem cells to delete exons 1-4 of the Tectb gene (Fig.1a,b).
checks.explanation: The paper describes deleting exons 1–4 of Tectb, as the claim says.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, Tectb protein was absent from the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Tectb was not detected in the tectorial membranes or epithelia of mice homozygous for this deletion
checks.explanation: Tectb protein was not detected in the tectorial membranes of homozygous mice.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, the striated-sheet matrix was missing along the whole length of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Transmission electron microscopy revealed a complete absence of striated-sheet matrix throughout the length of the tectorial membrane in Tectb−/− mutant mice
checks.explanation: The paper reports striated-sheet matrix was absent throughout the membrane's length.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, the tectorial membrane remained attached to the organ of Corti.
checks.evidence_quote: In the Tectb−/− mutant mice described in this study, the tectorial membrane remains attached to the organ of Corti
checks.explanation: The Discussion states the membrane stays attached to the organ of Corti.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, Hensen's stripe was absent.
checks.evidence_quote: there was a noticeable absence of Hensen’s stripe, a longitudinal ridge thought to engage the hair bundles of the inner hair cells
checks.explanation: The paper reports that Hensen's stripe was absent.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, the marginal band of the tectorial membrane was lost apically.
checks.evidence_quote: In the apical end of the apical coil, the marginal band was absent and the tectorial membrane had a markedly frayed peripheral edge in the Tectb−/− mutant
checks.explanation: The marginal band was absent at the apical end.

checks.claim: In Tectb-null mice, the apical tectorial membrane was about twice as thick as in controls.
checks.evidence_quote: The thickness of the tectorial membrane in the apical coil of the Tectb−/− mutant was twice that of the heterozygous or wild type mice (72.1±3.5 μm vs. 36.4±1.9 μm
checks.explanation: The apical tectorial membrane was twice as thick as in heterozygous or wild-type controls.

paragraphs.text: Russell et al. (2007) found that Tectb-null mice had a low-frequency hearing loss below about 20 kHz, with reduced distortion product otoacoustic emissions in that range. At higher frequencies, neural sensitivity was close to normal, and basilar membrane and neural tuning were sharper than in wildtype mice. The authors attributed the sharper tuning to a reduced acting mass of the tectorial membrane and weaker longitudinal coupling along the cochlea.

checks.claim: Tectb-null mice had low-frequency hearing loss below about 20 kHz.
checks.evidence_quote: The enhanced high-frequency tuning in the Tectb−/− mutant mice, therefore, came at the expense of a hearing loss for frequencies below 20 kHz
checks.explanation: The paper reports hearing loss below 20 kHz.

checks.claim: Tectb-null mice had reduced distortion product otoacoustic emissions at frequencies below about 20 kHz.
checks.evidence_quote: Even with the highest levels of primaries used in these experiments, DPOAE levels in the frequency region below 20 kHz were 20–30 dB less than those recorded from wild type mice
checks.explanation: DPOAEs below 20 kHz were reduced compared with wild-type mice.

checks.claim: At higher frequencies, neural sensitivity in Tectb-null mice was close to normal.
checks.evidence_quote: For frequencies above ~ 20 kHz, however, neural sensitivities in wild type and Tectb−/− mutant mice were very similar.
checks.explanation: Neural sensitivity above about 20 kHz was very similar to wild type.

checks.claim: At higher frequencies, basilar membrane tuning in Tectb-null mice was sharper than in wildtype mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Although these mice have a low-frequency hearing loss, basilar-membrane and neural tuning are both significantly enhanced in the high-frequency regions of the cochlea, with little loss in sensitivity.
checks.explanation: Basilar membrane tuning was sharper in the high-frequency regions; the measurements were made at the 53 kHz place.

checks.claim: At higher frequencies, neural tuning in Tectb-null mice was sharper than in wildtype mice.
checks.evidence_quote: Simultaneous masking neural tuning curves closely resemble the tuning properties of single auditory nerve fibers and are more sharply tuned in Tectb−/− mutant mice than in wild type mice
checks.explanation: Neural masking tuning curves were sharper than in wild-type mice.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) attributed the sharper tuning in Tectb-null mice to a reduced acting mass of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: These findings can be attributed to a reduction in the acting mass of the tectorial membrane and reveal a new function for this structure in controlling interactions along the cochlea.
checks.explanation: The authors attribute the findings to a reduced acting mass of the tectorial membrane.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) attributed the sharper tuning in Tectb-null mice to weaker longitudinal coupling along the cochlea.
checks.evidence_quote: This novel role for the tectorial membrane in determining the frequency resolution of the cochlea can be attributed to a reduction in the strength of longitudinal mechanical coupling within the tectorial membrane.
checks.explanation: The authors attribute the sharper tuning to weaker longitudinal coupling. They place it within the tectorial membrane and describe its effect as reduced interaction along the cochlea.

paragraphs.text: Russell et al. (2007) concluded that Tectb is required to form the striated-sheet matrix of the tectorial membrane. Without Tectb, alpha-tectorin still formed disorganized filaments but did not form an organized striated-sheet matrix. This suggested that Tectb may cross-link filaments based on Tecta.

checks.claim: Russell et al. (2007) concluded that Tectb is required to form the striated-sheet matrix of the tectorial membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Tectb is therefore essential for formation of the striated-sheet matrix and may act as a cross-linker of Tecta-based filaments.
checks.explanation: The authors conclude Tectb is essential for forming the striated-sheet matrix.

checks.claim: In the absence of Tectb, alpha-tectorin still formed disorganized filaments.
checks.evidence_quote: indicating that Tecta can, in the absence of Tectb, form filaments but is unable to form organised striated-sheet matrix
checks.explanation: The paper says Tecta can still form filaments without Tectb; these are described as disorganised 8 nm filaments.

checks.claim: In the absence of Tectb, alpha-tectorin did not form an organized striated-sheet matrix.
checks.evidence_quote: indicating that Tecta can, in the absence of Tectb, form filaments but is unable to form organised striated-sheet matrix
checks.explanation: The paper states Tecta cannot form organised striated-sheet matrix without Tectb.

checks.claim: The Tectb-null mouse findings suggested that Tectb may cross-link filaments based on Tecta.
checks.evidence_quote: Tectb is therefore essential for formation of the striated-sheet matrix and may act as a cross-linker of Tecta-based filaments.
checks.explanation: The paper proposes that Tectb may cross-link Tecta-based filaments.

references.label: Russell et al. (2007)
references.citation: Russell IJ, Legan PK, Lukashkina VA, Lukashkin AN, Goodyear RJ, Richardson GP. Sharpened cochlear tuning in a mouse with a genetically modified tectorial membrane. Nat Neurosci 10: 215-23, 2007. [PubMed: 17220887]
